summary: A Yes vote continues an existing one-eighth-cent (0.125%) countywide special sales tax, providing about $15.5 million annually until ended by voters, to fund regional and neighborhood parks, water supply and habitat protection, wildfire risk reduction, and trails, with community oversight and annual audits.

tax.text: A Yes vote extends the Measure M sales tax to continue funding parks and park improvements.
tax.quote: This measure extends the Measure M sales tax, which was passed by voters in 2018 and sunsets in 2029.

tax.text: A No vote does not extend the Measure M sales tax beyond its scheduled 2029 sunset.
